sections.h2: Where is the Yadkin tax counter, and what are the payment options?
sections.html:
The Yadkin County Tax Department is in Yadkinville, and its tax office page places the in-person payment counter in the Magnolia building across from the courthouse at 101 South State Street. The office line is 336-849-7903.

Four payment routes are listed:

  • Online, through the county's bill lookup and payment site.
  • By telephone at 866-249-4184, where you need the year and bill number.
  • In person at the Magnolia building.
  • By mail to Yadkin County Tax Department, P.O. Box 1217, Yadkinville NC 27055, with a printed copy of the online bill.

The same page says to contact the office for address changes, value changes and general questions, and to consult an attorney for deed work.

sections.h2: How big is Yadkin County and who lives there?
sections.html:
The county spans roughly 335 square miles of land, with about 111 residents on each, per Census QuickFacts. Its 2025 population estimate is 38,325, a 3.0% gain over 2020.

  • Owners occupy 76.9% of homes, the 2020 to 2024 rate, which suggests many households stay in place.
  • Census puts the typical owned home at $181,200 and typical rent at $766.
  • Household income in the middle is $62,932.
  • About one resident in four and a half is 65 or older (22.4%), so age-based relief matters here.
  • Workers average a 29.6 minute trip to their jobs.

The county issued 116 building permits in 2025 by the Census count, so new construction is modest and resale homes dominate.

sections.h2: Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?
sections.html:
Yes. The tax office's page announces that a 2027 revaluation is underway. State law puts every county on a cycle of at most eight years, and the county's 2023 reappraisal notices are posted in its document center.

Revaluation changes the assessed value of each parcel to its market value as of the new January 1 date, and the county follows the uniform appraisal standard in G.S. 105-283, which describes true value as the price a willing buyer and willing seller would agree on. Owners in a reappraisal year often see bigger changes than usual, and the review window is the time to compare the new notice with recent nearby sales.

Ask the tax office when notices will be mailed and how to reach an appraiser. The county also keeps a reappraisal appeal form in its online form center.

sections.h2: When are Yadkin County taxes due, and is there an early discount?
sections.html:
The county tax page offers a 2% discount for paying in August, ahead of the September 1 due date set by G.S. 105-360. Interest starts after the grace period that ends the day before January 6.

The same page lists solid waste fees: $76.00 per household, $38.00 for a household with the elderly exemption, and $10.00 for extra stickers. Those fees are separate from the value-based tax, so a seller should ask whether they have been paid up at the time of closing.

Whoever held title at year start is billed.

sections.h2: Where does a Yadkin County value dispute go?
sections.html:
Start with a call or email to the tax office, which handles value changes, and take a formal case to the county's review board if that fails. The commissioners usually serve as that board under G.S. 105-322.

The statute lets a taxpayer ask for a hearing in writing or in person before the board adjourns, and the board mails its decision within 30 days after adjourning. In a reappraisal year the board calendar runs longer than usual, so ask which dates apply. Owners with a stronger case should bring recent sale prices of similar homes nearby, photographs and repair estimates.

Beyond the county, the Property Tax Commission takes a written notice filed within 30 days of the mailed decision (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What relief programs exist for Yadkin County owners?
sections.html:
The Yadkin tax office takes applications for state exemptions and exclusions. These three use NCDOR's 2026 figures, and only one can be used at a time.

North Carolina relief programs open to Yadkin County owners
ProgramQualificationBenefit
Elderly or disabled exclusionAge 65 plus or fully and permanently disabled, income no higher than $38,800 for 2026Greater of $25,000 or 50% of value excluded
Disabled veteran exclusionQualifying veterans and unmarried surviving spouses, no age or income testFirst $45,000 of value excluded
Circuit breakerSame age or disability test, five years living in the home, income up to $58,200Tax capped at 4% or 5% of income, excess deferred

The form is AV-9, filed with the county assessor and accepted through June 1 (NCDOR; G.S. 105-277.1).

sections.h2: Which Yadkin County desk answers which question?
sections.html:
The tax office page splits its contacts into three email links: one for assessor and payment matters, one for appraisal, and one for exemptions. Use the appraisal link for a value question and the exemptions link for relief forms, so the message reaches the right staff member quickly.

Owners can also pull printable parcel maps from the county's GIS site and download property record cards from the tax page. A record card shows what the county has on file for a house, so check it for errors in square footage or condition before a buyer's appraiser does. Deed questions belong with an attorney and the Register of Deeds, which the tax page links to separately.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Yadkin County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Settlement takes it from the seller's side. Because the lien is dated to the first of the year (G.S. 105-355), a sale does not wipe it out, and an unpaid parcel can be collected through a courthouse auction.

Request a payoff amount that includes solid waste fees before you list, and pass it along to the closing attorney. Rural land can carry extra layers, so ask for the whole parcel record.

sections.h2: How should a Yadkin County seller handle solid waste fees and listing rules?
sections.html:
Count the $76.00 household fee among the yearly carrying costs of a Yadkin property. A purchaser's lawyer may want proof that stickers and fees are current, so check with the tax office.

Business personal property, such as tools or equipment kept at a rental or workshop, is listed in January. G.S. 105-307 runs the listing period from the first working day of January through its end, and commissioners may extend it. Individuals with good cause may request more time in writing. Anything not listed can draw a penalty, so ask the office how to list.

sections.h2: Which Yadkin County timeline matters most before listing a home?
sections.html:
Plan backward from the first day of September. A seller who plans a fall or winter closing should confirm the bill status in August, when the 2% discount applies, and again before the end of the year.

Yadkin County tax dates from the county page and state law
DateEvent
January 1Ownership and value fixed for the year
January 1 to 31Personal property listing
August2% early payment discount
September 1Taxes due
January 6Interest begins

Buyers and sellers usually split the bill by closing date, and the attorney's settlement statement should show the split.

faqs.q: What is the Yadkin County tax office phone number?
faqs.a: The number is 336-849-7903. The counter serves walk-ins on weekdays, with the day ending at 5:00 pm.

faqs.q: Does Yadkin County offer an early payment discount?
faqs.a: Yes, a 2% discount applies when taxes are paid in August, according to the county's tax page. Confirm the current terms with the office.

faqs.q: Can I pay Yadkin County taxes by phone?
faqs.a: Yes, call 866-249-4184 and have the year and bill number ready.

faqs.q: When is the Yadkin County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county's tax page says the 2027 revaluation is underway. Ask the office when notices will be mailed.

faqs.q: How much is the Yadkin County solid waste fee?
faqs.a: The county page lists $76.00 per household and $38.00 for households with the elderly exemption, with additional stickers at $10.00.
